title: UPVSS: Jointly Managing Vector Similarity Search with Near-Memory Processing Systems
problem: Vector similarity search is bandwidth-bound in CPU-based systems; DRAM bandwidth becomes the critical bottleneck as data scales, limiting throughput in recommendation systems and LLM deployments.
motivation: Modern applications (LLMs, recommendations) demand efficient similarity search; conventional von Neumann architectures cannot saturate compute due to memory bandwidth limitations.
method: Offloads similarity search to UPMEM near-memory processing units, distributing computation close to data to reduce core-to-memory data movement and maximize UPMEM's parallelism through architecture-aware workload distribution.
key_novelty: Architecture-aware integration of vector search with UPMEM's distributed PIM capabilities to overcome bandwidth bottlenecks.
contributions: Intelligent operation prioritization for PIM vs CPU
System-level performance improvements for real-world search workloads
limitations: Not discussed; scope limited to UPMEM integration without general PIM architecture exploration.
